## F06 Hooks and lifecycle events

- F06.event-catalog — Event catalog [supported, unverified] Hooks run scripts on tool and session lifecycle events, such as before or after tool calls. Listed events include `PreToolUse` (a tool is about to run; the only blocking event), `Stop` / `StopFailure` (a turn ends, or ends with an API error) and `SubagentStart` / `SubagentStop` (a subagent starts or finishes). | ev: E-grok-build-00257, E-grok-build-00259, E-grok-build-00364, E-grok-build-00383
- F06.handler-types — Handler types [supported, unverified] A hook is a shell command or HTTP endpoint that Grok calls when a lifecycle event occurs. `type` is `"command"` or `"http"` (with a `url` to POST the event to); `timeout` is in seconds, default 5. | ev: E-grok-build-00252, E-grok-build-00255, E-grok-build-00383
- F06.input-contract — Input contract [supported, unverified] The event arrives as JSON on stdin (`hookEventName`, `sessionId`, `cwd`, `workspaceRoot`; for tool events `toolName` and `toolInput`). Every hook process also receives `GROK_HOOK_EVENT`, `GROK_HOOK_NAME`, `GROK_SESSION_ID` and `GROK_WORKSPACE_ROOT` in its environment. Plugin hooks additionally receive `GROK_PLUGIN_ROOT` and `GROK_PLUGIN_DATA`. | ev: E-grok-build-00260, E-grok-build-00302
- F06.output-blocking — Output and blocking semantics [partial, verified] Exit code 0 allows, exit code 2 denies; only an explicit `deny` blocks. For passive events, stdout is ignored; exit 0 on success. | limit: `PreToolUse` is the only blocking event. Everything else, including timeouts, crashes and malformed output, is fail-open: the failure is recorded in the session but the tool call proceeds. | ev: E-grok-build-00261, E-grok-build-00257
- F06.matchers — Matcher semantics [supported, verified] `matcher` is a regular expression tested against the tool name (Claude tool names such as `Bash`, `Read`, and `Edit` are mapped to Grok's automatically); omit it to match everything. | ev: E-grok-build-00254
- F06.config-locations — Configuration locations [supported, unverified] Hooks are JSON files: personal hooks in `~/.grok/hooks/*.json`, project hooks in `‹project›/.grok/hooks/*.json`; extra roots via `~/.grok/hooks-paths`. Claude Code (`.claude/settings.json`) and Cursor (`.cursor/hooks.json`) hook files are read as well. Plugin hooks additionally receive `GROK_PLUGIN_ROOT` and `GROK_PLUGIN_DATA` in their environment. | ev: E-grok-build-00253, E-grok-build-00303, E-grok-build-00302
- F06.trust-enable — Trust and enable controls [supported, verified] Project hooks require trust before they run: the first time you open a repo with hooks, grant it with `/hooks-trust` or by launching with `--trust`. The decision is stored in `~/.grok/trusted_folders.toml` and covers project MCP and LSP servers too. Loaded hooks can be managed and inspected in the `/hooks` tab of the extensions modal. | ev: E-grok-build-00256, E-grok-build-00255

## F12 MCP

- F12.client-support — Client support [supported, unverified] MCP servers expose external tools to Grok; once configured, their tools are available alongside the built-in ones, namespaced as ‹server›__‹tool›. The grok mcp ‹list|add|remove|doctor› subcommand manages MCP servers. | ev: E-grok-build-00262, E-grok-build-00226
- F12.transports — Transports [supported, verified] The url field of an [mcp_servers.‹name›] entry is an HTTP/SSE MCP endpoint. | ev: E-grok-build-00077
- F12.config-scope — Config location and scope [supported, verified] Servers can be declared in ~/.grok/config.toml or in a project .grok/config.toml (repo-shared MCP, plugins, and permission rules); a project server with the same name as a user one replaces it entirely. Grok also loads MCP configs from ~/.claude.json, .cursor/mcp.json, and project .mcp.json, merged below config.toml in priority. | ev: E-grok-build-00146, E-grok-build-00267, E-grok-build-00269, E-grok-build-00271
- F12.auth — Authentication [supported, unverified] bearer_token_env_var injects an Authorization: Bearer header from an environment variable. Servers that require OAuth trigger a browser flow on first use, with tokens stored under ~/.grok/mcp_credentials.json. Remote servers can use a static auth header (--header is repeatable). /mcps authenticates OAuth servers with i. | ev: E-grok-build-00078, E-grok-build-00268, E-grok-build-00265, E-grok-build-00270
- F12.tool-filtering — Tool filtering and naming [supported, unverified] MCP tools are available alongside the built-in ones, namespaced as ‹server›__‹tool›. GROK_TOOL_SEARCH (1/0) gives on-demand MCP tool discovery for large toolsets; [features] tool_search (true/false, default on) controls MCP tool search / discovery. | ev: E-grok-build-00262, E-grok-build-00068, E-grok-build-00207
- F12.server-trust — Server trust and approval [supported, unverified] Project hooks require trust before they run: grant it with `/hooks-trust` or by launching with `--trust`. The decision is stored in `~/.grok/trusted_folders.toml` and covers project MCP and LSP servers too. | ev: E-grok-build-00256

## F13 Sessions, checkpoints, rewind

- F13.resume-continue — Resume and continue [supported, verified] `-r, --resume [‹ID›]` resumes a session by ID, or the most recent if omitted; `-c, --continue` continues the most recent session for the current directory. In the TUI, `/resume` opens a picker of recent sessions for the current workspace. | ev: E-grok-build-00091, E-grok-build-00294, E-grok-build-00092, E-grok-build-00137
- F13.fork-branch — Fork or branch a session [supported, unverified] `/fork [directive]` branches the current session into a peer that starts from a copy of the conversation; `--worktree` or `--no-worktree` chooses whether the fork runs in an isolated copy of the repository. When resuming, `--fork-session` forks into a new session ID. | ev: E-grok-build-00297, E-grok-build-00005, E-grok-build-00050
- F13.checkpoint-rewind — Checkpoint and rewind [supported, unverified] `/rewind` (or `Esc Esc` while idle) lists a rewind point per prompt; selecting one restores all files to their state at that point and truncates the conversation to match. Rewind modifies files on disk — reverted changes are lost unless committed to git. | ev: E-grok-build-00299, E-grok-build-00049, E-grok-build-00319
- F13.transcript-storage — Transcript storage [supported, verified] Grok saves every conversation to disk automatically (prompts, responses, tool calls, file snapshots) under `~/.grok/sessions/`, keyed by working directory; `GROK_HOME` (default `~/.grok`) is the home for sessions, among other things. `grok export ‹session-id› [output]` exports a session transcript as Markdown. | ev: E-grok-build-00293, E-grok-build-00223, E-grok-build-00061
- F13.session-listing — Session naming and listing [supported, unverified] `grok sessions ‹list|search|delete›` lists, searches, or deletes sessions; `grok sessions search ‹query›` searches session titles and prompts. `/rename ‹title›` renames the current session (alias `/title`), and `/sessions` switches, renames, or closes active sessions. | ev: E-grok-build-00222, E-grok-build-00379, E-grok-build-00381, E-grok-build-00136
- F13.cross-surface-handoff — Cross-surface handoff [partial, verified] Grok saves every conversation to disk under `~/.grok/sessions/`, keyed by working directory. Sessions work the same in the TUI, headless mode, and over ACP. | limit: Sessions are saved under `~/.grok/sessions/`, keyed by working directory. | ev: E-grok-build-00293

## F14 Worktrees and parallel execution

- F14.worktree-isolation — Worktree isolation [supported, unverified] A worktree session runs in an isolated copy of your repository, so parallel agents cannot overwrite each other's files. Worktrees require a git repository, live under `~/.grok/worktrees/‹repo›/‹name›`, and start from your current HEAD, including uncommitted changes. `-w, --worktree [‹NAME›]` starts the session in a new git worktree. | ev: E-grok-build-00126, E-grok-build-00006
- F14.concurrency-caps — Concurrency caps [partial, verified] At most 50 scheduled tasks can be active at once. Loops expire after 7 days; the interval accepts Ns (minimum 60), Nm, Nh and Nd. | limit: The cap is stated for scheduled tasks only: 'at most 50 scheduled tasks can be active at once'; the quote gives no limit on concurrent agents or sessions. | ev: E-grok-build-00246
- F14.parallel-subagents — Parallel subagents [partial, verified] Subagents spawn independent child sessions that handle tasks in parallel. Workflows orchestrate a bounded set of background subagents (fan out, verify, return a result) and are on by default. Subagents can request worktree isolation when the parent delegates parallel work. | limit: GROK_SUBAGENTS ('Enable subagents / the task tool') defaults to 0 (E-grok-build-00066), while Workflows, which use subagents, are 'on by default' (E-grok-build-00329); these quotes do not settle whether subagents are enabled out of the box. | ev: E-grok-build-00306, E-grok-build-00329, E-grok-build-00044, E-grok-build-00066
- F14.total-agent-caps — Total agent caps [undocumented, verified] swept for: max(imum)?.{0,15}(turns|steps|agents|calls|iterations|subagents); (limit|cap)s?.{0,30}(agents|calls|turns|steps|subagents|iterations); up to \d+ (agents|subagents|turns|steps|calls); hits 1, reviewed 1; positive control `grok`: 349 hits
- F14.multi-session-coordination — Multi-session coordination [supported, unverified] The Agent Dashboard is a fullscreen overview of every session: which agents need input, which are working, and which are done. Open it with `/dashboard` or `grok dashboard`. Permission prompts and questions can be answered inline with the number keys. | ev: E-grok-build-00249, E-grok-build-00363, E-grok-build-00348

## F15 Background, scheduled and cloud-delegated work

- F15.background-tasks — Background tasks [supported, verified] Grok runs commands, subagents and monitors in the background while the conversation continues. Ctrl+B sends the running command to the background; /tasks lists background tasks, subagents and scheduled tasks. [toolset.bash] auto_background_on_timeout (default true) backgrounds a command on timeout. | ev: E-grok-build-00242, E-grok-build-00052, E-grok-build-00321, E-grok-build-00161

The interval accepts `Ns` (minimum 60), `Nm`, `Nh`, and `Nd`; the prompt fires immediately, then repeats, and each firing is a new agent turn. Cancel from the tasks pane, or ask the agent to. | limit: Loops expire after 7 days, and at most 50 scheduled tasks can be active at once. | ev: E-grok-build-00246, E-grok-build-00051

## F16 Surfaces and programmatic control

- F16.interactive-cli — Interactive CLI [supported, verified] Running `grok` with no arguments starts the interactive TUI, a rich, mouse-interactive, fullscreen experience. `[ui] screen_mode` is `fullscreen` (default when unset) or `minimal`, the default render mode for plain `grok` (restart required); `--no-alt-screen` runs inline (no alternate screen / fullscreen TUI takeover). | ev: E-grok-build-00219, E-grok-build-00397, E-grok-build-00166, E-grok-build-00090
- F16.headless-mode — Headless mode [supported, unverified] Grok Build can be used headlessly in scripts or bots. `--output-format ‹FMT›` chooses `plain`, `json`, or `streaming-json`; streaming JSON emits incremental events as they arrive. For CI/CD and headless automation, set the `XAI_API_KEY` environment variable — no config file needed. | ev: E-grok-build-00001, E-grok-build-00216, E-grok-build-00103, E-grok-build-00333
- F16.ide-integration — IDE integration [supported, unverified] Use ACP when you want IDE or tool integration rather than a terminal session. Grok Build can be used through the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) in other apps, and `grok agent stdio` runs it as an ACP agent over stdin/stdout. | ev: E-grok-build-00217, E-grok-build-00333, E-grok-build-00227
- F16.desktop-web-app — Desktop and web apps [undocumented, verified] swept for: desktop app; web app; browser (version|interface); standalone app; mobile app; hits 0, reviewed 0; positive control `grok`: 349 hits
- F16.sdk-api — SDK and API [supported, unverified] `grok agent stdio` runs Grok as an ACP agent over JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout. `session/prompt` returns completion metadata; the assistant text itself arrives as `session/update` chunks. | ev: E-grok-build-00218, E-grok-build-00227

## F19 Modes and autonomy levels

- F19.named-modes — Named modes [supported, verified] Shift+Tab cycles Normal, Plan, Auto (when available) and Always-approve. The [ui] permission_mode setting accepts default, ask, auto or always-approve. | ev: E-grok-build-00024, E-grok-build-00318, E-grok-build-00185
- F19.entering-modes — How modes are entered [supported, verified] Shift+Tab cycles Normal, Plan, Auto (when available) and Always-approve. /plan [description] enters plan mode (active on the next prompt). /auto toggles auto mode when the feature is enabled. /always-approve or grok --always-approve enters always-approve. | ev: E-grok-build-00024, E-grok-build-00027, E-grok-build-00132, E-grok-build-00318
- F19.plan-mode — Plan mode [partial, verified] In plan mode only the session plan file can be edited until you approve, independent of permission mode; the plan review is not skipped under auto or always-approve. The agent can enter plan mode on its own; leave with Shift+Tab when idle or q on the approval screen. | limit: Plan mode gates edit tools, not the shell — bash can still write via redirection. Reads, bash, and MCP still follow permission mode. | ev: E-grok-build-00029, E-grok-build-00028, E-grok-build-00047, E-grok-build-00111
- F19.autonomy-mode — Auto-accept and autonomous modes [supported, verified] Auto uses a classifier to auto-approve safe tools; dangerous ones may still prompt. Always-approve skips permission prompts for tool calls (/always-approve, Shift+Tab or grok --always-approve). Deny rules and hooks still apply; auto and always-approve do not skip plan review. | ev: E-grok-build-00022, E-grok-build-00132, E-grok-build-00278
- F19.read-only-mode — Read-only or ask mode [partial, verified] GROK_WRITE_FILE (default 1) set to 0 disables the write tool, described as for read-only sessions. | limit: Env var disables the `write` tool ("read-only sessions"); the quote does not describe a named read-only mode or cover other file-changing tools. | ev: E-grok-build-00067
- F19.mode-defaults — Mode defaults and persistence [partial, verified] [ui] permission_mode takes default, ask, auto or always-approve as the default tool-permission behavior. Legacy keys approval_mode and yolo = true still work; permission_mode wins when more than one is set. Plan mode stays on until you approve or quit. | limit: Default in user config only (`~/.grok/config.toml` or managed/requirements — not project `.grok/config.toml`). | ev: E-grok-build-00025, E-grok-build-00185, E-grok-build-00279, E-grok-build-00026
